title: Evaluating Type-1 Diabetes Digital Twins by Decision Quality
abstract: arXiv:2610.30577v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A digital twin (DT) for type 1 diabetes (T1D) can predict how an individual's blood glucose will respond to different insulin treatments without actually trying them. For each treatment, downstream statistics of predicted glucose trajectories, such as glycemic risk, can be computed to guide clinical decisions. However, the quality of DTs is usually measured by the accuracy of their predicted glucose trajectories, which may not reflect the quality of the downstream treatment decisions they inform. In this work, we directly evaluate DTs by this decision quality on downstream treatment ranking, i.e., whether a DT predicts glucose trajectories that can be used to rank candidate treatments as the real patient would. We present an evaluation protocol over 30 virtual patients from the FDA-accepted UVA/Padova model, each simulated under 21 different basal-bolus treatments. translated_title: 基于决策质量的1型糖尿病数字孪生评估
translated_abstract: 1型糖尿病（T1D）的数字孪生（DT）可以预测个体血糖对不同胰岛素治疗方案将如何响应，而无需实际尝试这些方案。对于每种治疗方案，可以计算预测血糖轨迹的下游统计数据（例如血糖风险），以指导临床决策。然而，数字孪生的质量通常是通过其预测血糖轨迹的准确性来衡量的，这可能无法反映其所支撑的下游治疗决策的质量。在本工作中，我们直接用下游治疗方案排序的决策质量来评估数字孪生，即数字孪生所预测的血糖轨迹能否像真实患者那样用于对候选治疗方案进行排序。我们提出了一套评估协议，涵盖来自FDA认可的UVA/Padova模型的30个虚拟患者，每位患者在21种不同的基础-追加（basal-bolus）治疗方案下进行仿真。对于每个患者，数字孪生在一种治疗方案下拟合，然后生成血……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出不再以血糖轨迹预测精度、而是以下游治疗方案排序的决策质量来评估1型糖尿病数字孪生，并基于FDA认可的UVA/Padova模型中30个虚拟患者、21种基础-追加治疗方案建立了系统的评估协议。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes evaluating type-1 diabetes digital twins by decision quality—whether their predicted glucose trajectories can rank candidate treatments as the real patient would—rather than by trajectory prediction accuracy, presenting an evaluation protocol over 30 virtual patients from the FDA-accepted UVA/Padova model simulated under 21 different basal-bolus treatments.
